title.narrative: Minska undernäring och hunger hos barn, unga flickor och kvinnor i DRK
Reducing malnutrition and Hunger in children, adolescent girls and women in DRC

description.narrative:
Phase I
- Through cash transfers improve levels of food security and dietary diversity for household members especially children.
- Through cash transfers increase household livelivehoods, incomes and resilience.
Phase II
- Strengthen the enabling environment for improved maternal, child and adolescent nutrition.
- Improve access to high impact nutrition services for children aged 0-23 months, adolescent girls and women.
- Develop and integrate early childhood development interventions into community nutrition packages.
- Strengthen community engagement to improve nutrition, health and hygiene practices, demand and service utilisation as well as mote investment in the food systems approach.

Insatsen stödjer ett multisektoriellt nutritionsprogram med en ”cash transfer” komponent, med syftet att minska undernäring och hunger i Demokratiska republiken Kongo. Den främsta målgruppen är barn, unga flickor och kvinnor. Det fyraåriga programmet kommer att genomföras i provinserna södra Kivu, Kasai och Kwilu. Programmet bygger vidare på den nationella multisektorala strategiplanen för nutrition (2016-2020) och kompletterar både det nationella nutritionsprogrammet (PRONANUT) och Världsbankens nutritionsprogram.

The contribution aims to support a multisectoral nutrition package with a component of cash transfers, to reduce malnutrition and hunger, and promote sustainable diets, services and practices in the DRC. The main target group will be children, adolescent girls and women. The 4-year programme will be implemented in South Kivu, Kasai and Kwilu Provinces. The programme builds on the National Multisectoral Strategic Plan for Nutrition (2016-2020) and complements both the national nutrition programme (PRONANUT) and the World Bank nutrition programme.

Results from the contribution include:
Phase 1
-4,805 recipients across 23 villages in six health areas received cash transfers.
-According to surveys 80% of recipients report a higher frequency of meals and 53% say that their family now consumes healthier meals after receiving the transfers.
-Dairy consumption showed a dramatic increase, rising from 7% at baseline to 45%. Similarly, legumes and meat consumption also saw substantial increase, increasing from 77% to 100% and 74% to 99%, respectively.
-An expansion in reported frequency of consuming protein-rich foods and dairy. Hence not only more veriety of food groups but also frequency. For young children and mothers (particularly those who are pregnant or breastfeeding) this can have significant impact on their well-being.
-Cash transfers have been used by households to build houses, health expenses, food, clothes, buying land, paying debt and loans, investing in exisiting businesses and also starting new businesses.
Activities continue without Sida funding until december 2026 by Give Directly to reach the total amount of months of cash transfers planned for.
Phase 2
-Activities implemented in 5 health zones in Kasai, 10 health zones in Kwilu and 6 health zones in South Kivu
-Six Territorial Multisectoral Nutrition Committees have been set up and are functional.
-288,000 packs of 30 sachets of micronutrient powders procured and distributed to implementing partners in the Sud Kivu and Kwilu provinces and 11,195 cartons of lipid based nutrient supplements small quantities distributed in the Kasai province.
-Communication materials on maternal, early child development and adolescent nutrition have been distributed to 21 health zones of the three provinces of implementation.
-During the first six months of 2025, a total average of 99,273 children under 2 attended monthly preschool consultations, while 41,349 children aged 24 to 59 months visited on a quarterly basis.
-39 847 children received food fortification(micronutrient powders and lipid based nutrient supplements small quantities)
-339 culinary demonstrations were organized at health facility level to train women on optimal utilization of local foods and cooking process to preserve micronutrients.
-Iron folic acid supplementation for the prevention of anaemia were supplied to 105 447 pregnant women and 30,608 adolescent girls in the 3 provinces.
-2233 women support groups and men's groups set up and operating in Sud Kivu, Kasai and Kwilu provinces
-Support to the development of communication and training material on early child development has been given.
-39,627 children attended stimulation spaces
-306 baby-friendly spaces built in health facilities in Sud Kivu, Kasai and Kwilu
-170 health personnels trained on early child development
-96,988 people sensitized in communities on different topics related to nutrition: 58,797 people in Kasai, 21,331 in Kwilu and 16,860 in South Kivu.
-During the reporting period from January to June 2025, 8,570 children under 5 years old were treated for severe acute malnutrition and discharged from the hospital as cured.
-Training on women and girls groups on nutrition has contributed to the creation of community fields and livestock breed which is positive for local food production.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
